comparison: Perfect agreement on experimental design and data generation (C3, C38-C43). Both evaluations find the methods clearly documented with appropriate sample sizes and quality control. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on cell type identification and compositional analysis (C44-C52). Both accept the annotation methodology and validation. OpenEval notes technical confounders were appropriately acknowledged; peer reviewer requests additional validation of fresh vs. frozen differences but accepts the core finding. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on the common NE signature (C53-C59). Both accept the validation in bulk RNA-seq data and functional enrichment. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on the two SiNET subtypes (C4, C60-C75). Both evaluations recognize this as a major finding supported by multiple lines of evidence and validated in bulk samples. OpenEval emphasizes the technical rigor; peer reviewers explicitly affirm the finding as a strength. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on fibroblast heterogeneity (C76-C82). Both accept the identification of ABC transporter-expressing CAFs as novel. Peer reviewer requests methodological clarification but does not challenge the result. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on endothelial heterogeneity (C83-C85). Both accept the identification of Endo2 signature. Peer reviewer requests methodological clarification but does not dispute the finding. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on B cell proliferation in SiNET2 (C86-C88). Both accept this observation as part of the broader B cell proliferation pattern. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on minimal NE cell proliferation (C5-C6, C89-C98). Both recognize this as a key finding with solid evidence. OpenEval emphasizes the contrast with SiAdeno control and consistency across platforms; peer reviewers note it as interesting and applicable to other NETs. Editor notes evidence is solid but would benefit from larger sample size. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on bulk data validation of proliferation patterns (C99-C102). OpenEval treats this as independent validation; peer reviewers incorporate it into their overall assessment of the proliferation finding. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on germinal center analysis (C103-C105). Both accept this as a partial explanation for B cell proliferation without challenging the finding. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on the perfect association between subtype and B cell proliferation (C7, C106-C108). Both accept the 100% concordance as reported. OpenEval notes the causal inference remains speculative; peer reviewers acknowledge the finding without challenge. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on MIF identification (C8, C109-C113). Both accept MIF as differentially expressed and upregulated in epithelial-like tumors. OpenEval notes the causal link to B cell proliferation is speculative; peer reviewers acknowledge the TME role including MIF. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer evaluation of therapeutic implications is UNCERTAIN (see R14/R5 pairing).

Agreement on B cell dynamics observation (C152-C153). OpenEval notes the inference of high cell death is logical but would benefit from direct measurement; peer reviewers incorporate this into their overall B cell proliferation assessment. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding therapeutic strategy (C9, C154-C156, C158). Both evaluations find the therapeutic implications speculative. OpenEval notes lack of functional validation; peer reviewers express concern about clinical correlation and note lack of clear biological interpretation. Both rate as UNCERTAIN.

Agreement on mixed tumor analysis (C10, C116-C129). Both accept the identification of intermediate populations with stemness markers. OpenEval notes this is well-supported but N-of-1; peer reviewers find it intriguing but tangential and limited by single case. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer evaluation of broader implications is UNCERTAIN (see R16/R6 pairing).

Agreement on uncertainty regarding progenitor cell model for MiNENs (C11, C130-C131, C145-C146, C161). Both find the interpretation as bipotent progenitors speculative. OpenEval notes the hypothesis is plausible but not definitively supported; peer reviewers express reservations about generalizability and relevance due to N-of-1 nature. Both rate as UNCERTAIN.
OpenEval contextualizes proliferation findings and discusses Ki67 interpretation (C133-C136). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific contextual claims.
OpenEval discusses alternative explanations for low proliferation paradox (C137-C141), all marked as speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific hypotheses.
OpenEval draws parallels to oligodendroglioma and other cancer types (C142-C143, C147). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific comparisons.

OpenEval proposes TME-driven oncogenesis model (C148-C151). Peer reviewers address therapeutic implications of MIF/TME interaction with concern about clinical correlation. OpenEval rates model as SUPPORTED with speculative functional consequences; peer reviewers rate therapeutic implications as UNCERTAIN.

OpenEval summarizes main findings about two subtypes and minimal NE proliferation (C157, C159-C160). No corresponding peer review evaluation found as a separate summary assessment, though these findings are addressed in other peer review results.
OpenEval validates background information and context (C1-C2, C12-C37). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing background claims.
OpenEval cites recent related work for context (C132). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this citation.
OpenEval describes proliferation patterns in mixed tumor (C144). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific claim separately from the broader mixed tumor analysis.

Partial overlap on technical considerations. OpenEval notes both fresh and frozen samples in epithelial-like subtype (C66, C75); peer reviewers specifically request demonstration that cell type frequencies are not affected by sample processing methods. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN pending additional validation.
